_comment: Jungle art sources. The jungle was the only zone in the game drawn entirely
with fillRect primitives — 168 of them, and zero drawImage calls. This maps
the packs onto the JG tile enum so drawJGTile can draw real art.
Sheets are cut by connected opaque region, then sorted largest-area first.
Each entry is [index, "WxH"]: the index selects the sprite, the size is
checked against it so a pack revision that reorders sprites fails the build
loudly instead of silently mapping a rock onto a tree.
Separate-file packs (the Rocky pack ships PNG/Objects_separately/ exactly
like the desert pack) are listed by filename instead.
TROPICAL CAVEAT: no pack delivered so far has palms, banana leaves or
buttress roots. These are temperate-rainforest species standing in. Swapping
in a tropical pack later is an edit to this file, not to the renderer.
Strips are animation frames cut at a fixed pitch: the campfire's five frames touch, so a connected-region cut returns them as one blob.
Tiles are fixed 32x32 crops used as ground fill, drawn at the tile's top-left with no anchor offset — unlike sheets/files/strips, which anchor bottom-centre and overhang upward.

caveFungus is for Mine Floor 4 (The Unmapped), not the jungle — it shares this atlas because it comes from the same pack and the loader is already wired. Kept visually distinct from biolum: wall-growing crystalline fungi rather than the jungle's capped ones.

fishing_huts._note: One hut, not two. The pack draws its full house twice at (12,12) and (132,7) and the two crops are pixel-identical, so asking for both gave the village a second variant that did not exist. Its roof-only and wall-only pieces are distinct but are components, not standalone huts. The settlement reads as one design because that is what the pack has — same hands, same materials, which suits it.

campfire._note: Frames 0-1 are unlit logs; 2-4 are the burning loop.

fishing_dock._note: Deck interior. Both crops measured seamless (seam cost 0.60) so the dock tiles without a visible grid.

dungeon_ruin._note: Masonry for the Altaverde ruins' walls. The pack's floors are autotiled panels with no clean fill, so ruin flooring reuses DHGround's 'street' instead.
